status: private-execution-contract; not a public ABI or product/provider admission
selection: A compiled composition explicitly selects CachedObservations. The ordinary product keeps Fake. No input graph, option, environment variable or retrieved data selects admission. Observation focus stores its exact evidence ID separately: target_id is null, observation_id is retained, scope is observation-only. Missing observations stay missing at that exact ID until clear or explicit selection; repeated names or later captures never rebind focus. Fake peers retain their existing media identity checks and target selection.
publication: Only the selected graph profile is accepted. Validate graph and prepare media identity history before atomic publication. Observation IDs are not lifetime media identity tombstones. Source polling returns a retained immutable graph pointer without provider calls; acknowledge it only after successful publication. Frontend publication epochs and provider capture/worker epochs remain separate.
cached_actions: Inspect, list, topology and capability explanation over this private composition return org.disked.cached-observation-view/1 results marked cached-observations. Ordered target_ids contain only fake peers; ordered observation_ids contain only evidence nodes. Inspection preserves the exact node and binding. None authenticates a provider or supplies storage authority. Cached observation capability explanations retain unknown physical identity/freshness/permission/qualification and unavailable storage provider/recovery. Execution eligibility and authorization remain false.
storage_boundary: health.assess on an observation returns observation_not_storage_target, exit 3, without invoking the health port. Unsupported commands remain command_unavailable. GUI/TUI target form defaults never use observation focus. Shell completion offers observation IDs only for cached target.inspect/capability.explain, never for health or other target parameters. Manual external dispatcher inputs still require their own admission; display does not confer authority.
presentation: Use the existing frontend session, TUI, Win32 GUI and shell models. Headers and private rows distinguish cached observations from fake media. Underlying original names and returned-byte receipts remain lossless; visible text uses the existing inert ASCII JSON escaping. A display classification neither authenticates a producer nor changes transport limits. Stale actions return revision_conflict before lookup. Navigation/view state does not restart or retire a reader.
required_checks: Default composition rejects observation graphs without creating a reader.
Actual owned namespace and metadata observations preserve code/request/process/context/name/receipt bindings through direct service and GUI/TUI/shell model inspection.
Observation selection never supplies a storage target; health port remains uncalled and forms/completion preserve the distinction.
Identical names in later captures give new evidence IDs; old focus stays missing, stale actions conflict and retained old views stay immutable.
Rejected publication preserves source pointer eligibility, view epoch and selection; retry uses that same retained pointer.
More than 1024 observation identities do not consume media tombstones; fake identity reuse and the separate media history limit still reject.
Maximum selected private graph/display workloads run under the actual frontend memory job. Oversized/invalid graphs reject atomically; private display limits do not enlarge protocol output limits.
Existing product command, graph, frontend and native regression tests remain passing; exact source/build/host/import/artifact evidence is retained.
